external_entities.name: Supplier
external_entities.description: Suppliers upload compliance paperwork and sign in to the portal.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

external_entities.name: Category manager
external_entities.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.

external_entities.name: Vendor
external_entities.description: The vendor hosts the SaaS portal and pushes nightly supplier data extracts.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

processes.name: Portal
processes.description: A vendor-hosted SaaS product through which suppliers upload paperwork and category managers review and approve or reject it.
processes.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal

processes.name: Supplier master service
processes.description: Loads the nightly supplier data extract and writes records into the supplier database.
processes.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file and writes the records into the supplier database.

data_stores.name: Vendor platform
data_stores.description: The vendor's platform where supplier compliance documents remain.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.

data_stores.name: Landing bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket in the organisation's cloud account receiving the nightly supplier data extract.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_stores.notes: The runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is.

data_stores.name: Supplier database
data_stores.description: The database into which the supplier master service writes supplier records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The service and the database are all in our cloud account.

data_flows.name: upload paperwork
data_flows.description: Suppliers upload insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff to the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers upload their compliance paperwork through a portal — insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for their own staff.
data_flows.data_description: Insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for suppliers' staff.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Suppliers sign in to the portal using credentials issued by the vendor.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Suppliers sign in with a username and password that the vendor issues to them.

data_flows.name: review paperwork
data_flows.description: Category managers review uploaded paperwork and approve or reject it through the portal.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network, review what has been uploaded and approve or reject it.
data_flows.data_description: Uploaded compliance paperwork and associated contact details.

data_flows.name: store paperwork
data_flows.description: The portal stores supplier compliance documents in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The documents themselves stay in the vendor's platform.
data_flows.data_description: Compliance paperwork and supplier staff contact details.

data_flows.name: push extract
data_flows.description: The vendor pushes a nightly supplier data extract to the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every night the vendor pushes a supplier data extract to a landing bucket in our cloud account.
data_flows.notes: The extract was described as encrypted end to end, but the landing-bucket runbook says the file arrives as a plain CSV and is picked up as-is. These are conflicting positive claims, so encryption in transit is unknown.

data_flows.name: load extract
data_flows.description: The supplier master service loads the nightly extract from the landing bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our supplier master service loads that file

data_flows.name: write records
data_flows.description: The supplier master service writes the extracted records into the supplier database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: writes the records into the supplier database
data_flows.data_description: Supplier records from the nightly extract

trust_boundaries.name: Vendor platform
trust_boundaries.description: The vendor-controlled hosting environment for the SaaS portal and its documents.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The portal is a SaaS product. The vendor hosts it and we do not run any part of it.

trust_boundaries.name: Corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which category managers work.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our category managers, who work from the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: Cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account containing the landing bucket, supplier master service, and supplier database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The bucket, the service and the database are all in our cloud account.

assumptions.assumption: The vendor platform's contents are confidential because it holds compliance paperwork and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The store is stated to contain insurance certificates, food safety audits, and contact details for staff.

assumptions.assumption: The landing bucket's contents are confidential because it receives the supplier data extract containing supplier records and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The bucket receives the supplier data extract, which contains supplier records derived from the stated compliance paperwork and contact details.

assumptions.assumption: The supplier database's contents are confidential because it holds supplier records derived from compliance paperwork and staff contact details.
assumptions.basis: The database receives the records written from the supplier data extract, whose stated subject matter includes supplier and staff information.
